description: A choice, widely cultivated saprotroph that fruits in shelving clusters on dead hardwood. Fast, forgiving and beginner-friendly to grow — one of the most-produced mushrooms in the world.
edibilityNotes: A choice edible; always cook thoroughly. Generally beginner-friendly, but see the toxic jack-o'-lantern lookalike below — true oysters grow shelf-like on wood with decurrent gills running down a short off-centre stem, never in gilled clumps from soil/roots.
substrate: Dead and dying hardwood — beech, poplar, oak, willow
Logs, stumps and standing dead trunks
distribution: Cosmopolitan across temperate and subtropical forests worldwide; one of the most widely cultivated mushrooms.
capColor: variable: bluish-grey, tan, fawn, or near-white

dangerousLookalikes.name: Omphalotus olearius
dangerousLookalikes.note: Jack-o'-lantern — toxic, causes severe GI illness. Orange throughout, true gills (not oyster-like ridges), grows in tufts from buried wood/roots, and is faintly bioluminescent.
